note: This scene IS the claim 'relative coordinates resolve per aspect', and it has now refuted itself three times. (1) x:60/w:1800, absolute pixels tuned for a 1920 canvas, so 9:16 cut 'ratio.' off the frame. (2) The fix for that: pin:center with NO w. resolveCoords sizes a missing w as 0, so `center` resolved to (W-0)/2 and put the layer's LEFT EDGE on the centre line. It rendered jammed into the right half at EVERY aspect, 16:9 included, and passed the audit only because the ink still landed inside the safe box there. (3) dy:-190 / dy:20 to separate the two lines. dx/dy are ANCHOR offsets (scene.html reads them only when `anchor` names another layer), so with no anchor both were silently dropped and both lines rendered at the same y, overlapping. One lesson per bug: pin CENTRES A BOX, so a text layer needs w for there to be a box, and align for the text to centre inside it; dy without anchor is a no-op; and a vertical gap between two lines must come from `anchor`+`at`, not a percentage, because px-sized text in a %-placed box drifts as the canvas changes shape. All three were caught by `make audit ASPECT=all` plus looking at the frame. None were caught by rendering at 16:9. (4) The film STATED the claim and never showed it. A ratio is a SHAPE, so the shape is the explanation: the `frame` layer draws one rectangle that morphs 16:9 -> 1:1 -> 9:16 on the scene clock while the SAME five elements inside it re-resolve. The corner chip holds 26px off the top-left corner, the centre stack keeps its 72/50/34 percent of the width, the caption bar and the ratio label hold 26px off the bottom edge. Nothing inside is re-authored between the three shapes; only the box changes, which is the whole claim. Geometry is CSS (x/y/width/height are CSS properties on a rect in Chrome) driven off var(--t) in seconds, so it seeks like everything else; the attribute values are the settled 16:9 state and exist only as a fallback.
